question: Does KiCadRoutingTools route the same placements better than Copper?
method: Same stripped boards as copper_vs_designer_reference_boards_20261127.json; KiCadRoutingTools 0.24 (commit 192216e, prebuilt Rust router) autoroute.py; both routers' boards judged by KiCad 10.0.8 DRC with --refill-zones, errors compared by type with the designer's own board.

autoroute.track_check: VIN 389 C and DXL_VDD 332 C rise at 5 A and 2.5 A: unsafe

route_py_with_widths.track_check: 11.8 C and 8.2 C: the same as HS's own board

result: KiCadRoutingTools finished every board: SNAP clean, IP5328P with every connection made (Copper left 2), PiUPS adding 1 short and 1 clearance error against Copper's 7 shorts and 30 mask bridges, all in under 2 minutes. Its whole-board autorouter caps power nets at 0.3 mm, which passes DRC but would overheat HS-BUS-A's 5 A rail; called through route.py with the net-class widths it matches HS's own tracks. HS uses it that way, after FreeRouting and before Copper.
limits: Three 2-layer boards and one HS board; default settings otherwise; DRC-clean is not signal-integrity or thermal sign-off.
